the adaptive local polynomial regression estimator is optimal in the sense that it achieves the same rate of convergence as in the case of the known location of a discontinuity, and that the estimator is very sensitive to the presence of a jump, in the sense that its performance is essentially the same for a jump of size as for the case when the location of the jump is known.

the local polynomial regression with an adaptive window selection is near-optimal for the estimation of a regression with discontinuities or a regression with jumps and that the estimator is highly sensitive to the discontinuities or to jumps of a regression function or its derivatives.

the adaptive estimation of regression functions with discontinuities or jump discontinuities, in the case of the first derivative, is possible with a rate of convergence which is optimal for a smooth function, and which is very close to optimal for the function with discontinuies.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the classical approach of local polynomial regression with adaptive window selection can be used as a robust and computationally simple tool for the estimation of discontinuous functions and change points The proposed methodology can be applied to a variety of problems in the fields of economics and finance where discontinuities are common and the estimation is based on a limited amount of data
the local polynomial regression with an adaptive window can be a powerful tool for the detection of discontinuities in the regression function

a simple local polynomial fit with a window size chosen in a data driven way is able to detect and estimate change points and to provide an accurate estimate of the underlying function in the vicinity of these points The proposed methodology is implemented in the R package adaptpol and the package is illustrated by means of an application to the analysis of the effect of temperature on the survival of the European corn borer
